harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired consumer.py on node1. A single consumer now survives producer disconnects, blocks without busy-looping, records only complete non-empty lines, preserves existing records, and exits cleanly on SIGTERM. The repair and data survived the mandatory node reboot; RHEL 10, kernel, SELinux, and SSH remained unchanged and healthy.
actions_performed: Diagnosed and reproduced the original EOF/disconnect failure in an isolated sandbox.
Installed a Python 3.12-compatible FIFO reopen loop while preserving ownership, executable mode, and SELinux label.
Created a root-only rollback copy at /root/consumer.py.pre-fifo-repair.
Tested multiple successive producers, blank lines, unterminated fragments, idle CPU behavior, record retention, and SIGTERM exit status.
Safely rebooted node1, proved its boot identity changed, and repeated the workflow after recovery.
Removed temporary files and confirmed no test consumer process or test residue remained.
Final received.txt contains seven complete records (73 bytes), including its byte-for-byte original 13-byte prefix.

evidence.summary: Established RHEL/Python environment, ownership, permissions, security state, original checksums, source defect, and reproduced consumer exit followed by a blocked second producer.
Shows the installed source, successful syntax validation, preserved metadata/SELinux label, unchanged received data, and secured original-script backup.

evidence.requirement: Successive producers, complete non-empty lines, retained records, no busy loop, clean SIGTERM
evidence.summary: Pre- and post-reboot live tests show exact accepted records, ignored blank/partial records, preserved prefixes, sleeping FIFO wait with zero CPU-tick growth, and SIGTERM exit code 0.
Captures boot ID, SSH health/listener, source and data checksums, FIFO metadata, syntax, and preserved original data prefix.
Records native safe-reboot scheduling and the old boot identity.
Proves command recovery with a new boot ID and fresh uptime.
Shows unchanged OS/kernel, recovered SSH, persisted code/data checksums and FIFO metadata, followed by successful post-reboot FIFO behavior.
Confirms cleanup, final workflow success, enforcing SELinux, active SSH, preserved original prefix, final checksums, no remaining consumer, and no temporary residue.
